description: The single declaration of the daemon's serialised wire surface, shared byte-identically by both repos (P8-cb). Every field is classified: must_be_read (a production read site must exist), inert (nothing reads it, with the reason), not_assertable (the name is too common for a name-based check to prove anything), or unmodelled (no GUI slot, with the reason). The classification is exhaustive by test, so adding a field forces the choice (AU-d).

structs.note: WIRE-ag / DEC-331. Pinned from the first release that publishes it rather than after a divergence: WIRE-h is what an unpinned new struct costs. `label` is genuinely read (it is the Rail column) but is excluded from must_be_read by test_must_be_read_names_are_distinctive — the name is too common to prove a read site; tests/test_wire_ag_voltages.py asserts it at the call site instead. `id` has no GUI consumer yet, and the wire identity is modelled anyway because the model mirrors the wire; `channel` is read only as a display sort key.

DEC-333 §7. `verdict` and `blocking` together decide whether Start is offered — `preflight_view` reads BOTH, deliberately, so an unknown verdict token still fails safe on the field that gates a hardware-perturbing action. `header_id`/`diagnostic` are echoed identity.

Until daemon 2.52.0 the three readings were always null (read from the wrong JSON paths) and `result` was never stored; `services/validation_view.py::verify_evidence_detail` renders the token through `verify_view.outcome_for`.
